clue.text: Sanction brother's housing permits

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it inside, so one word is lodged within the other

blocks.note: BRO is short for brother, with the possessive S kept
to OK something is to sanction or approve it

explanation.surface: A brother's house being granted official permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanction' looks like the definition at the front, but it supplies the inner letters; the definition sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate or allow it, usually in the negative: he brooks no argument.

clue.text: Nomogram cut short by surprise

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

blocks.note: taken aback means taken by surprise

explanation.surface: A chart abruptly curtailed without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An abac is a technical term for a nomogram, a chart that solves equations graphically by lining up scales.

clue.text: Flora perhaps covering edges of Ifton Heath, for one

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, so only the first and last are kept
something covering another wraps around it, so one set of letters encloses the other

blocks.note: Flora Robson was a celebrated English actress; 'perhaps' marks her as one example of the surname
the outside letters of the place name

explanation.surface: A woman named Flora wandering over a stretch of heathland near the village of Ifton.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath reads as moorland in the surface, but it is a first name: W. Heath Robinson was the cartoonist of absurd contraptions.
explanation.definitionFit: W. Heath Robinson, the English cartoonist famed for elaborate contraptions, is one person bearing this surname.

clue.text: Skilful exploit carrying most of credit

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter, so the tail is trimmed
a bearer carrying a load has it on board, so the one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: buying on tick means buying on credit
a deed or feat

explanation.surface: A clever stunt that earns its performer most of the praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'exploit' as being carried by the shortened credit word. TACTIC as an adjective is a rare dictionary form of tactical, and the fit with skilful is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, tactic is a dictionary variant of tactical, describing adroit planning and manoeuvring.

clue.text: Fanatic leader standing on crate

blocks.note: a head is a leader or chief
both crate and banger are British slang for a decrepit old car

explanation.surface: A zealous leader climbing on a box to address the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the first piece stands on the second. A crate here is a battered old car, not a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A headbanger is informal for a wild extremist or zealot, as well as a heavy-metal fan.

clue.text: Musical in which very good French article mentioned Mr Simpson

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the letters are those of a word as it is pronounced

blocks.note: OK signals approval
la is the feminine 'the' in French
Homer Simpson of the cartoon, pronounced without the final R in a British accent

explanation.surface: A stage show in which a French newspaper item praised Homer Simpson.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone only works in a non-rhotic accent, where Homer ends in an unvoiced R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodgers and Hammerstein's first stage collaboration, from 1943, is named after the American state.

clue.text: Massage succulent plant around source of spots?

indicators.note: turned around, the plant's name is read from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: to massage is to rub
aloe is a fleshy-leaved succulent

explanation.surface: Rubbing aloe vera gel on a pimple to soothe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of spots' looks like a mere surface detail, but it is the definition, with a question mark for its playful indirectness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubeola is the medical name for measles, an illness that covers the body in a red rash.

clue.text: Hiking gear regularly chopped to make type of fire

indicators.note: chopping at regular points removes the letter in the same position of each word

blocks.note: a back pack, with the opening letter of each word cut off

explanation.surface: A rucksack hacked into kindling for a campfire.
explanation.walkthrough: Hiking gear is BACK PACK; regularly means the same position, here the first letter, goes from each half.
explanation.definitionFit: Ack-ack is old military slang for anti-aircraft gunfire, from the signallers' alphabet for the letters AA.

clue.text: At specific intervals, regularly sarky about number one

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means every other one, here the even-placed letters
about means surrounding, so the kept letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
number one is nursery talk for urinating, also called a wee

explanation.surface: Someone repeatedly being sarcastic about the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Number one looks like the boss or top dog, but it is the children's euphemism. Sarky is British slang for sarcastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Used after a frequency, as in twice a week, the phrase sets out a regular recurring schedule.

clue.text: Football is certainly this unfair

blocks.note: literally true: football is a different sport from cricket
the idiom for unsporting or dishonourable conduct

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic reading taking the idiom literally; cricket is the English bat-and-ball game long held up as a model of fair play.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom calls dishonourable or unsporting behaviour by the name of the game associated with gentlemanly conduct, negated.

clue.text: Literally relaxed face

indicators.note: taking the slang for relaxed literally, letter by letter, means writing the first word of it back to front

blocks.note: relaxed is laid-back, taken here as an instruction

explanation.surface: A calm, unruffled expression.
explanation.walkthrough: Relaxed is laid-back; taken literally, the word laid is put back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a clock or watch, marked with the hours, is called its dial.

clue.text: Best singles, those intended for audience not players

definitions.text: those intended for audience not players

blocks.note: on a vinyl record the main track was on the A-side

blocks.clueFragment: those intended for audience not players
blocks.note: remarks in a play spoken to the audience but unheard by the other characters

explanation.walkthrough: Players looks like musicians after singles, but it means actors on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical remarks addressed past the other actors share the spelling of the lead tracks on old pop records.

clue.text: Burn in hell with scold that's going over old ground?

blocks.note: Dis is the classical underworld
to char is to scorch
to row someone is to tell them off

explanation.surface: Someone tormented in hell by a nagging voice that keeps repeating the same old complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: Going over old ground sounds like rehashing a quarrel, but it is literal: a farm tool pulled over tilled land.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm implement with rows of concave steel blades breaks up soil already ploughed, travelling across the same field again.

clue.text: Chatty bird having no time to hug soft dog

indicators.note: having no means going without, so a letter is struck out
to hug is to wrap one's arms around, so the shortened bird encloses the letter

blocks.note: cockatoos are noisy, talkative parrots
T is the abbreviation for time
p for piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A talking parrot that never has a moment to cuddle a gentle dog.
explanation.definitionFit: This designer crossbreed mixes a cocker spaniel with a poodle.

clue.text: Prowling medic taking drugs

blocks.note: MO is a Medical Officer
using is slang for taking illegal drugs

explanation.surface: A doctor on the prowl, high on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting mice, as a cat does when it stalks around, is described by this present participle.

clue.text: Old engineer in operation to stop excessive current

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this piece is pushed into the middle of the other

blocks.note: OTT is over the top
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a live wire or system is switched on and working

explanation.surface: A veteran electrician at work fitting a circuit breaker against power surges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like it gives O, but it belongs to the definition; the O comes from over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Camillo Olivetti, an Italian engineer born in 1868, founded the typewriter company carrying his surname.

clue.text: Material page removed from grand plan

indicators.note: something removed from a word is taken out of it, so that letter disappears

blocks.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
a program, in the American spelling, is a plan of action
p is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A sheet torn out of an ambitious scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Grogram is a coarse fabric of silk mixed with mohair or wool, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: French painter unexpectedly arouses you at the climax

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out in a surprising order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A French artist stirs a viewer at the high point of a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the climax' puts the you-letter at the very end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Rousseau, the naive painter of jungle scenes such as The Dream, was a French artist.

clue.text: Execute present revelation

blocks.note: surface reading: carry out a current disclosure of secrets
setter's reading: the present is a gift, and revealing it means taking off its paper

explanation.walkthrough: Present looks like an adjective for now, but it is a gift; executing its revelation means opening it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off the paper around a gift brings the contents into view, so it is the act of revealing a present.

clue.text: A number of half-cut neighbours teeter with head fully down

indicators.note: cutting something in half throws away one half, so only the front half of each word survives
sending the head right down to the bottom moves the opening letter to the very end

blocks.note: the first half of the ten-letter word
the first half of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: Several tipsy neighbours swaying, then keeling over head first.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut looks like British slang for drunk and so an anagram, but it halves both words; then the leading N drops to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The cardinal following seventeen, ten plus eight, is a whole number.

clue.text: Children absorbed in self-instruction

indicators.note: something absorbed in a phrase is soaked up inside it, so the letters sit within those words

blocks.note: the run of letters inside the compound word

explanation.surface: Kids engrossed in teaching themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin is an old word for a small child or urchin, so elfins are little ones.

clue.text: Fraudulent suspect hiding terribly daft anarchy

indicators.note: hiding letters puts them out of sight, so they vanish from the word
done terribly, a word comes out in a mess, so the letters to be hidden can turn up in any order
a suspect arrangement is dubious and not to be trusted, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; 'terribly' says these letters come out in any order

explanation.surface: A dodgy suspect concealing a terribly foolish plot to cause chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D, A, F and T from fraudulent in whatever order they appear, and rearrange the six letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrule is an archaic noun for lawlessness, the absence of government or order.

clue.text: Improve visit

blocks.note: things ... when they get better
to look someone up is to call on them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to get better, as prospects do, and to drop in on an old acquaintance.

clue.text: Brand buttocks, right side then left

indicators.note: putting the right-hand side before the left swaps the two halves of the word

blocks.note: British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Branding cattle on the rump, one side and then the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To brand an animal is to burn a mark into its hide with a hot iron, which scorches it.

clue.text: Suggest warning party to block playwright

indicators.note: something put in to block a passage sits inside it, so this piece goes within the name

blocks.note: golfers shout fore to warn of a ball in flight
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish dramatist
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Proposing that a political faction warns against censoring a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow is to hint at or indicate something before it happens.

clue.text: Former US president minimally identified first victim

blocks.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's familiar first name
the surname reduced to its initial, the least that identifies him

explanation.surface: An ex-president barely recognised as the earliest casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: Abe L. is Abraham Lincoln identified as briefly as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abel, son of Adam and Eve, is killed by his brother Cain, the first murder in the Bible.

clue.text: Old character split when outside hospital

indicators.note: lying outside something means surrounding it, so the letters wrap the other piece

blocks.note: torn means ripped or split
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: An elderly patient, divided in mind, standing outside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Old character sounds like an elderly eccentric, but it is a letter of an old alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn is the runic letter used in Old English for the th sound, an obsolete written symbol.

clue.text: Apostle briefly wrapping brown bread for table

indicators.note: said briefly, the name is cut short and loses its final letter
wrapping means enclosing, so the shortened name goes around the other piece

blocks.note: St Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles
brown bread is Cockney rhyming slang for dead, and late means dead

explanation.surface: A saint wrapping a wholemeal loaf to bring to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown bread looks like food for the table, but it is Cockney rhyming slang: brown bread rhymes with dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is also a tableland, an area of high flat ground, which is what a plateau is.
